record.paper_title: Some open problems in dynamical systems
record.original_question: Let f be a smooth diffeomorphism of the cylinder T^1 × [−1,1] that preserves Lebesgue measure, is homotopic to the identity, has no periodic points, and whose boundary rotation number ρ(f|_{T^1×{−1}}) = α satisfies a Diophantine condition. Must f be smoothly C^∞-conjugate to the rigid cylinder rotation R_α(θ,r) = (θ + α, r)?

evidence.quote: 3.2 - Question. Letf be a C∞ -diﬀeomorphism preserving the Lebesgue measure of T1×[−1, 1], homotopic to the identity, that has a ﬁnite number of periodic points ... and is such that the rotation number ρ(f|T1×{−1}) = α satisﬁes a diophantine condition. Is f C∞ -conjugated to Rα(θ,r) = (θ+α,r) ?

artifact.category_tag: Smooth conjugacy / rigidity of area-preserving cylinder maps
artifact.status_search_result: Searches surface the classical Arnol'd–Herman–Yoccoz theory for circle diffeomorphisms with Diophantine rotation number (which are smoothly conjugate to the rigid rotation), but no source directly resolves the cylinder version stated here, where rigidity is asked from boundary data alone. The problem appears to remain open, but no definitive recent resolution was located.

status_evidence.title: Herman's theory revisited
status_evidence.snippet: Herman proved that any C∞ circle diffeomorphism with Diophantine rotation number is C∞-conjugate to the rigid rotation.
status_evidence.claim: The 1-dimensional analogue (circle case) is fully solved by Herman/Yoccoz, providing the motivation for the cylinder question.

status_evidence.title: Generic Rigidity for Circle Diffeomorphisms with Breaks
status_evidence.snippet: Rigidity for circle diffeomorphisms is guaranteed only when rotation numbers satisfy a Diophantine condition.
status_evidence.claim: Recent rigidity literature focuses on circle maps; no analogous theorem for cylinder diffeomorphisms with the stated hypotheses was found.
